name: Exact Complement Projection Fails Above Threshold One
definition: Let $C=\{0,1\}^3\setminus\{000,111\}$, take $t>1$ and $t<s<t^2$, and assign unnormalized rows $(1,1,1)$ and $(1,s,s^2)$ to its two missing patterns.
properties: After normalization the prescribed array belongs to $\mathcal A_t(C)$, but it has no lift to the symmetric complement relation: a complementary missing row would force both $b_1<t b_3$ and $s^2b_3<t b_1$, contradicting $s^2>t^2$. Both optimized coefficient ratios nevertheless equal one. Thus the exact prescribed-array projection theorem is sharp at threshold one.
